chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) liked Al-Zabibiyya.

key_terms.الزَّبِيبِيَّةُ: Al-Zabibiyya (a sweet dish of raisins and walnuts)

ai.seo_question: What was Imam al-Sadiq's favorite food?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi highlights the personal culinary preferences of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), illustrating the Shia concept of 'tawassu' (broadness in permissible matters) where the Imams enjoyed simple, wholesome foods without ascetic restriction. The dish, Al-Zabibiyya, typically a mixture of raisins and walnuts, reflects the dietary norms of the era and serves as a practical example of the Imams' engagement with daily life. This hadith is often cited to demonstrate that the Imams did not impose rigid dietary laws but rather endorsed moderate and enjoyable consumption of permissible foods.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws liked Al-Zabibiyya’ - (A sweet dish of raisins, and walnuts etc.).
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from abu Basir who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, liked Zabibiyah (a dish with raisins) quite well.’”
